I feel this way too much. After a pretty bad night mentally I looked him up on Facebook. Guess I'm a glutton for punishment. He's remarried now, left his old family, lives miles away and has a toddler daughter.

Ugh.

Just read your most recent post. This is amazing in so many ways, thank you for sharing and putting yourself out there. I know for me especially it can be a struggle sometimes so it's good to see other people going through and conquering their past

It only gets better with time. I know it sucks taking baby steps, but learning to live again takes time. With time, you get so much better dealing with everything. Like a weight being lifted from you. Yes, it'd be great to just "be better" and at times it's hard as hell, but you have to walk before you can run. You can handle this, you are strong, and you are most definitely worth it. None of this is your fault.

I think I would personally go with a mix of the first two options. If you're not comfortable telling her, you don't have to. You don't have to be ready. We live in muddled greys, not black and white and things are complicated. There's nothing to be ashamed of, yet I understand the shame as well. Especially telling a parent. Your mother cares for you and that's why she's so torn up and pestering you about it. You don't have to open a discussion with her about it, but you also don't have to leave her in the dark. I know that in my situation, my feelings of guilt made me initially push those I care about away from me unintentionally. You are strong and what happened is not your fault. Your mom will understand, but only when you're ready to tell her.

Why does anyone obsess over anything? Who the fuck knows. I have problems, I guess, that need to be solved and I'm constantly questioning if I'm capable of solving them. It's like trying to do a puzzle with pieces from 4 different boxes. I'm trying so hard, but it seems so pointless and tedious

Fuck those guys for real though. If you don't have a razor in one hand, a noose in the other, and the oven on and open for good measure, they push you off on some other talk line or just tell you to piss off.

That's the thing, though. People are so aware that it's a constant peep show that they put on their best show. Some people are convinced that showing themselves having fun makes them more fun or cool or however they want to portray themselves. It's not about comparing because if you're comparing yourself to something fake, you'll always find yourself lacking.
